title: Get Out of Your Lazy Bed
year_note: Wikipedia says January 1984; one fan source says February. The 12-inch (BIANCO 1T) is dated 1983 in the 2016 reissue notes.

notes.made: Mark Reilly and Danny White wrote it. Matt Bianco were three people at this point: Reilly singing, Basia Trzetrzelewska singing and arranging the vocal harmonies, and White on keyboards. John Buckley engineered this track and Phil Harding mixed it. Ronnie Ross plays baritone sax and Peter Ross plays drums and percussion.
notes.context: Reilly, White and Basia had just left Blue Rondo à la Turk, and named the new band after a made-up 1960s spy. It was their debut single on WEA and reached 15 in the UK, 8 in Ireland and 2 in Norway; the video puts them on a black-and-white chequered floor. The album followed on 10 August 1984, peaking at only 35 in the UK but going to number 1 in Austria. In New Zealand it became the theme of the kids' Saturday show What Now from the mid-1980s into the early 1990s. In 1985 Basia and White left to make records as Basia.

listen_for.note: That's Ronnie Ross, a British jazz veteran who had taught a young David Bowie and was the baritone soloist on Lou Reed's 'Walk on the Wild Side'.
Two lead voices: Reilly's and Basia's, with Basia arranging the harmonies. That's where the record's jazz side comes from, more than any instrument.

leads_to.title: Walk on the Wild Side
leads_to.why: Same baritone sax player, Ronnie Ross, twelve years earlier, taking the solo on a Bowie and Mick Ronson production.

notes.unverified: Producer is unclear: the song's Wikipedia page credits Peter Collins, but the album's credits give Collins only the B-side 'Big Rosie' and list Reilly and White as producers, so I left the producer out of 'made'. Panel quote (Folake): the album's Latin percussionist, Robin Jones, is credited on every track except this one (Peter Ross plays drums and percussion here), and I couldn't confirm a scat break. The UK top 20 claim is right (15).

culture.title: Number 2 in Norway
culture.line: The debut single reached 15 in the UK, 8 in Ireland and 2 in Norway. Its album went to number 1 in Austria.

culture.title: What Now theme
culture.line: New Zealand's Saturday kids' show What Now used it as its opening theme from the mid-1980s to the early 1990s.

culture.title: The chequered floor
culture.line: Pete Cornish's video has the band performing on a black-and-white chequered floor.
